summary: C.R.O.P. (Crop Rotation Over the Plains) is an essential decision-support tool that equips farmers with optimal crop rotation strategies, all validated by peer-reviewed research. By leveraging NASA data alongside straightforward farmer input, this tool recommends tailored crop rotations that align with each farmer's field conditions. It takes into consideration key factors such as profitability, crop health, field survivability, and water conservation. Farmers can choose the crop rotation that best meets their primary objectives while also addressing necessary maintenance considerations.
details:
Source Code: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12Wb92u6Ou0mM9EIoxJm40hID0pSFuVMG

CROP is a web platform that helps farmers make data-driven crop rotation decisions based on real-time conditions. By combining NASA satellite data with the farmer's own input, the tool recommends two optimal, peer-reviewed crop rotation strategies. It also makes execution easy by providing clear to-do lists and printable plans.

Designed especially for farmers in the U.S. High Plains, CROP helps them achieve their agricultural goals using scientifically proven methods with highly predictable outcomes.

Our core database of crop rotations comes from peer-reviewed agricultural research. We used Google Gemini to match real-time NASA satellite data with these research-backed conditions, bridging the gap between scientific theory and live farm data. Then, we used Claude to turn this complex backend into an intuitive, farmer-friendly user interface.

CROP stands out because it doesn't just dictate a solution. It explains why the chosen rotation is best, provides a step-by-step execution guide, and outlines what could happen if predictions change.

Finally, we know agriculture is subject to unpredictable events, no matter how accurate the forecasts are. To handle this, CROP includes a feature that models alternative scenarios, showing farmers exactly what their yield and farm would look like if unexpected weather or environmental shifts occur.
